chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'The testimony of women is accepted in marriage and not accepted in divorce.' And he said: 'If three men and two women testify, it is valid for stoning (al-rjam), but if two men and four women testify, it is not valid.' And he said: 'The testimony of women is accepted with men in blood (diyah/compensation).'

And that which further clarifies this is what was narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr from Asim from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of a boy against whom a woman testified that he had thrown a boy into a well and killed him, and he validated the woman's testimony as equivalent to a woman's testimony (i.e., half of a man's).
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for the validity of women's testimony in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details Imam Ali’s (AS) nuanced jurisprudence on women's testimony, distinguishing its validity in marriage contracts versus divorce proceedings and establishing specific gender ratios for capital punishment (rjam). It further confirms the acceptance of women's testimony alongside men in blood money (dam) cases, supported by a judicial precedent where a single woman's testimony was deemed equivalent to another's in a homicide dispute. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that the competency of testimony is context-dependent rather than uniformly restricted.
